rule.description: A file-scope function counts as having deeply inlined callee bodies when its body contains copied statement fragments (normalized against identifier/number/string renaming) of at least two distinct other functions of the same file, with fragments that are substantive (at least 5 matched statements and at least half of the fragment source's statements; at least 30 matched tokens and at least 40% of the fragment source's tokens) and laid out mostly contiguously (longest copied run of at least 6 statements). The rule is evaluated on top of a clang-tidy back-end pass (readability-function-size with a case-specific line threshold of 4) that semantically parses the unit and yields the per-function structural inventory used as the analysis gate.

checks.description: Detect file-scope functions whose bodies carry copies of other functions' body fragments instead of calling them.
checks.detected_relation: file-scope function -> copied body fragment of another file-scope function in the same file
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The assigned smell is a method whose sub-method implementations are copied into itself. A caller that embeds ordered, mostly contiguous statement sequences of two or more other functions is performing its callees' work itself; several of these relations nest (fragment of a helper inside a fragment of a mid-level routine), which is exactly the depth-expanded composition the smell describes.

The pair-nulling sequence inside the duplicate-pair removal reuses the same assignment idioms as the pair-release helper. The shared run is 3 statements with 32 matched tokens, below the rule's floors, so it is intentionally outside the rule.
The shared diagnostic-then-cleanup tail is upstream reuse; its copied run is 5 statements and 29 matched tokens, below the rule's floors of 6 contiguous statements and 30 tokens.

The command-line driven setter shares flag-composition statements with its caller-shaped helper boundary. The pair sits at 42 of 107 source tokens (below the 40% ratio floor is not met: 42 tokens < 42.8), so it falls outside the rule.
